title: One story, two breaths
lede: In 2025, Shikaku moves and speaks. Here is what is certain about the adaptation, and how we compare it with the 2014 manga pages.

compareTitle: What changes when the page starts to move

compare.title: Rhythm
body: In manga, readers set their own pace. Fujimoto's signature silent pauses work because we can linger on one empty panel before turning the page.
Animation takes control of time. A pause must be measured in seconds, so a quiet moment can feel longer, or more rushed, depending on direction. It is one of the most interesting things to watch for.

compare.title: Music and sound
body: Manga is silent, so explosions and gunshots only live in sound effects and speed lines. The adaptation gives everything a sound, including Shikaku's own voice through Kana Hanazawa.
For us, the biggest challenge runs the other way: how the anime protects silence. One scene without music can be as strong as one empty page.

compare.title: Scene choices
body: A one-shot has to fit inside one anthology episode. Every scene kept, compressed, or added is an editorial decision about what the story is really about.
While watching, notice which part gets the most room: the absurd murder attempts, or the TV broadcast at the end. That choice shows how the adaptation team reads Shikaku.
